verdict.rationale: Poke's Recipes let users build shareable set-ups: published recipes get a share link, and the set-up can bundle MCP-backed custom tools and data sources, a prefilled first message, and the context Poke needs from the user. These are shareable configurations of the single Poke assistant, not distinct custom assistants with their own persona or system instructions. missing for 10: true per-assistant custom instructions/persona, uploaded knowledge bases (beyond MCP data sources), evidence that a shared recipe behaves as a separate assistant, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can build and share custom assistants with their own instructions and knowledge

citations.quote: All new and existing users can use Poke Recipes to easily set up automations and integrations, as well as share their set-ups with others.
Publishing a recipe: marks it Published, generates a referral/share link, makes it eligible for payouts
Optionally set: What context Poke needs from the user (inputContext), Prefilled first message (prefilledFirstText)
Poke supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, allowing you to extend Poke with custom tools and data sources.
